static_traits.name: Chen Jie
static_traits.family_status: Married, no children yet; has ten nieces/nephews (nephews/nieces)
static_traits.social_status: Spousal support; a team background of working with fellow National Guard members, seen as needing to maintain a strong image, and usually rarely expresses vulnerability in front of fellow members
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no treatment history for similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logicality, able to cooperate in exploration; high self-demands with self-reproach; able to notice and describe emotions and bodily reactions

basic_info.main_problem: As Christmas approaches each year, feeling overwhelmed and Anxiety from needing to prepare gifts for ten nieces/nephews, believing I cannot afford it; this pressure worsens yearly, affecting sleep and physical/mental state, and causing Relationship tension with spouse.
basic_info.core_demands: The increasingly heavy holiday pressure and Anxiety is hard to bear; hoping for professional support to cope with these feelings more effectively.
growth_experiences: Since several years ago, pressure and Anxiety about gift-giving have started months before Christmas each year, pressuring myself to meet gift expectations; despite trying budgeting and planning, pressure persists and worsens yearly, affecting sleep and the relationship with spouse.

In a flood rescue mission, successfully rescued dozens of people with the team, but still could not save one trapped person in time, and has long repeatedly replayed the event, generating strong guilt and self-blame, accompanied by physical symptoms like chest tightness, rapid heart rate, and headache, and believing 'if I had been faster / more efficient, that person would have survived'.

core_beliefs: If I cannot meet others' expectations, it means I am a failure / incompetent
If the outcome goes wrong it is my responsibility; I should bear full responsibility for all consequences
Expressing vulnerability will be seen as weakness and looked down on

special_situations.event: Thinking as Christmas approaches that I need to prepare gifts for all ten nieces/nephews, but may be unable to afford it financially
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot prepare gifts for each younger relative, it means I disappointed the family and I am an incompetent elder
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Starting budgeting and planning months in advance, constantly pressuring myself to try to meet expectations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot afford it; they will be disappointed; I am a failure

special_situations.event: Recalling the situation in the flood rescue where one trapped person could not be saved in time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not saved everyone, it equals failure / incompetence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replaying details, blaming oneself harshly, setting higher standards to avoid 'failing' again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I had been faster, he would not have died; this is my responsibility

special_situations.event: Considers whether to express inner guilt and troubles to National Guard comrades
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express vulnerability, others will look down on me and think me incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Suppresses the need to express herself, choosing silence to maintain a 'strong' image
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am weak and not capable enough

special_situations.event: In the months before each holiday, mood starts rising and the worst consequences are repeatedly rehearsed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must cover everything; none can be left out, otherwise big problems will occur
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly planning, repeatedly weighing expenses and lists, but also Avoiding communicating with others about real difficulties
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot do it all, it equals complete failure and everything will be terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted, affirmed by others as a reliable caregiver/contributor
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing others, being evaluated as weak or incompetent, thereby being belittled and distanced
defense_goal: Avoids failure by maintaining high standards and self-reproach
Repressing vulnerability in front of comrades to maintain a 'capable/strong' image

object_relations.self_representation: A provider/rescuer who must always be strong and reliable, not easily making mistakes
object_relations.object_representation: Judgmental, high-expectation others (family/comrades) who will be disappointed in or look down on me because of my inadequacy

object_relations.self_representation: A person who easily blames self in relationships and takes full responsibility for outcomes
object_relations.object_representation: Important others easily disappointed or 'hurt/burdened' by me (such as a spouse, helpees)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about the segment of the disaster rescue where one person could not be saved, or being asked whether one can see the positive side
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding others' concern as a test of one's ability; admitting emotions equals being incompetent
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Steady tone, tending to narrate facts and details objectively and downplaying emotional words; when invited to feel emotions, shifting to discussing 'why it happened' and 'how it could be improved'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to express vulnerability to comrades or close others and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that expressing feelings will be seen as weakness, and thereby belittled or judged
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding briefly and displacing the topic, lowering emotional intensity; using phrases like 'nothing / I can handle it myself', avoiding staying with vulnerable experiences.

manifestations: Facing Death in the flood rescue and repeatedly replaying and blaming oneself over the one person who could not be saved
Intruded by related memories almost every day, hard to let go
outcomes: Somatic reactions such as chest tightness, increased heart rate, and headache

manifestations: Highly compliant with the inner rule 'must meet everyone's expectations', has difficulty setting bearable boundaries for herself (such as the scope and form of gift-giving)
outcomes: Worry and rumination starting months before festivals

manifestations: Unwilling to show vulnerability in front of comrades, worrying about being seen as weak or incompetent
outcomes: Fewer opportunities to seek peer support
Increased emotional burden, inner self-blame cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and self-reproach, involving excessive self-restriction, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Harshly judging oneself with high standards to avoid being judged
Worrying that expressing vulnerability will appear incompetent

contact_model.definition: The individual turns energy originally meant to be expressed outward against the self, doing it to oneself, or restraining behavioral impulses directed at others.
manifestations: Suppresses the urge to ask fellow servicemembers for help and express vulnerability
Turns failure and anger into self-blame and self-reproach

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Presets that peers will look down on oneself and think one is weak
Chooses silence and avoids expressing emotions accordingly

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse and can communicate worries
Strong helping motivation and sense of responsibility; having saved many people in rescues
Willing to seek help and accept professional support
Has tried concrete strategies like budgeting and planning
Work performance not yet significantly affected, basic life functions maintained
negative_force: Self-reproach and a tendency to take all responsibility onto oneself
Catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, and prophetic worry lead to long-term stress
Avoiding expressing vulnerability in front of comrades, reducing opportunities to obtain support
Rumination and physiological stress responses accumulate months before festivals
Internalizing others' expectations as rigid 'shoulds', with insufficient boundary-setting for oneself

target_behavior.behavior: Pre-holiday Anxiety and catastrophic worry about gift-giving (with insomnia)
antecedent: The approaching holiday and related prompts (shopping, budgets, family-and-friend gathering topics)
Thinking about needing to prepare gifts for all ten nieces/nephews and possibly being unable to afford it
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing others' expectations as standards that must be met, framing the situation with the belief 'achieving all = qualified; not yet achieving = failure'
target_behavior.function: Avoids the risk of being seen as rude/disappointing others, trying to gain a sense of control through excessive worry and planning
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent anxiety and Sleep impaired; Relationship tension with spouse, worsened physical and mental burden

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated rumination and self-blame over the rescue incident (accompanied by chest tightness, increased heart rate, headaches)
antecedent: Thinking about details of the flood mission and the one person who could not be saved
Related cues (news, disaster topics, team memories)
target_behavior.core_reason: Attributing outcomes beyond individual control to personal inadequacy, thereby maintaining the belief structure 'I am responsible for all outcomes'
target_behavior.function: Using self-blame and rumination to avoid directly facing the pain of powerlessness and chance, maintaining a subjective sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent guilt and physiological stress, worsening emotional distress, affecting daily rest and well-being
